parties:
Nurul Alam @ Shaheb Miah ------ Accused-Petitioner (on bail)

full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J: This Rule was issued upon an application under section 561(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong to show cause as to why the proceedings of GR case No. 387 of 2006 arising out of Bakulia Police Station Case No.5 dated 6-6-2006 under sections 406, 420 and 109 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Chittagong should not be quashed. 

 2. The facts of the case, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah was accused in GR No. 387 of 2006 arising out of Bakulia PS Case No.5 dated 6-6- 2006 under sections 406/420/109 of the Penal Code and 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. A split charge-sheet had been submitted by the investigation officer. The accused, who had issued the cheques were charged under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and the accused petitioner was charge-sheeted separately for an offence under sections 406/4201109 of the Penal Code. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the proceedings of Gk No. 387 of 2006 was stayed in its entirety. When this matter was brought to the notice of the trial Court, an application was made on 25-1-2009 by one Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah for adding him as party in the instant Criminal Miscellaneous case stating that he was the real Nurul Alam, who was accused in that case and that he did not file the Criminal Miscella- neous Case before this Court upon which the Rule was issued. On 10-2-2009 the learned advocate who filed the Criminal Miscellaneous application, filed an application for withdrawing his power, which he had filed on behalf of the accused petitioner. By order dated 12-2-2009 another Bench of this Hon'ble Court was pleased to yacate the order of stay. The said order further indicates that the learned advocate Mr Md Ziaur Rahman, who had filed the Criminal Miscellaneous Petition, had informed the Court that he had sent his clerk to the address given by the tadbirkar but no one was found at that address and the tadbirkar was not available. By the same order, the matter was adjourned for 3 weeks for learned advocate Mr Md Ziaur Rahman to contact his client in order to ascertain the fact which has come into controversy and to inform this Court in this regard. From a subsequent order dated 2-7-2009 it appears that the learned advocate Mr Md Ziaur Rahman reported that he had written a letter to the tadbirkar and send it by registered post, but there was no reply and that his clerk had also gone to the address of the tadbirkar, but could not find any one named Md Shafiqur Rahman (which is the name of the tadbirkar). On the other hand, it transpires that Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah (the applicant to be added as party) alleged that Md Shafiqur and Md Abdus Salam, having forged his signature, used his name in filing the instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case before the High Court Division. 

 3. The learned advocate Ms. Afroza Nazneen Akhter, who had filed the application for addition of party on behalf of Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah informed the Court that instruction had been withdrawn from her and filed an application to surrender her power. The learned advocate Mr Lokman Karim filed a fresh power annexing a no objection certificate from Afroza Nazneen Akhter, to conduct the case on behalf of the application to be added as opposite party. 

 6. After due inquiry the' Additional Registrar-Z submitted his report after taking oral evidence from Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah and all the learned Advocates, who had been engaged by him in the past to conduct the various matters. Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah was identified by the witnesses at the inquiry, including the Principal Officer of Islami Bank Ltd. Agrabad Branch, Chittagong who filed the Artha Rin Suit No.27 of 2006 and GR No.387 of 2006. Nurul Alam denied having engaged learned advocate Md Ziaur Rahman. The sum and substance of the report is that the learned advocate Md Ziaur Rahman accepted the brief from one Md Shafiqur Rahman (tadbirkar) whom he did not know personally and he had no way of knowing the signature on the Vokalatnama of the person named Nurul Alam. It is further stated that Md Shafiqur Rahman and Md Abdus Salam were not available to be examined in the inquiry. The Additional Registrar could not come to any conclusion as to whether the person before him claiming to be Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah, who is accused in GR No. 387 of 2006 is in fact the same Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah, who filed the Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 14221 of 2007 either by himself or it was filed by someone else, who had forged his signature. 

 8. The learned advocate Mr Lokman Karim appearing in support of the application for addition of party confirmed before us that he is the engaged lawyer for Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah in GR No. 387 of 2006 and that his client did not file the Criminal Miscellaneous case numbered as Criminal Miscellaneous case No. 14221 of 2007. 

 9. While dealing with this matter we have perused the records relating to Writ Petition No. 11 of 2006; Writ Petition No. 2223 of 2007 and Writ Petition No. 1171 of 2009, we have also perused the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10425 of 2006, which was filed by Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah praying for ad-interim anticipatory bail in connection with GR No. 387 of 2006. 

 12. In the absence of Md Shafiqur Rahman, who was the tadbirkar in the instant Criminal Miscellaneous case, it is not possible to ascertain the motive behind filing it. It is also not possible to find out at whose behest the Criminal Miscellaneous case was filed. 

 13. Be that as it may, the stay having been vacated and the accused Nurul Alam alias Shaheb Miah confirming that he did not file the Criminal Miscellaneous case, the Rule is infructuous and accordingly it is discharged. 

 14. Before we part with this matter, we must put on record the activities of the learned advocates of the Bar in taking instruction from tadbirkars without ascertaining their identity. This is not expected from learned members of the Bar and is totally unacceptable. We find from the petition in the instant case that Mr Md Ziaur Rahman, learned advocate identified the deponent namely the tadbirkar of the case as being known to him and identified by him. The learned advocate Md Ziaur Rahman candidly submits before us that the tadbirkar was not personally known to him and that he did not verify his identification. This is a mockery of the system. Such activity of the learned advocate is highly deprecated. He is warned that this type of action will not be tolerated and he must be more careful in future. The Bench and the whole judicial structure depend so much on the integrity and alertness of the learned advocates of the Bar. Learned advocates must refrain from putting their signature identifying persons whom they do not know.
